newsitem.title: USA: Analyst shocked at AT&T earnings revision.
newsitem.headline: Analyst shocked at AT&T earnings revision.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Monday shocked analysts with a sharp downward earnings revison for 1997.
AT&T said it expected to earn $3.45 - $3.75 from core businesses in 1997 from $4.06 earned in 1996. It also said that new ventures would remove another $0.75 - $1.00 per share from 1997 earnings.
"The earnings targets are incredibly low compared to what we expected," said Frank Governali of CS First Boston.
Analysts had been expecting $3.25 - $3.45 per share including all dilutive costs.
AT&T also said that first quarter earnings in 1997 would be as much as 10 percent below the $0.76 per share earned in 1996's fourth quarter.
"It was somewhat of a shock," said Richard Toole, an analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Analysts said that AT&T by announcing $2.6 billion of cost cuts over the next two years seemed to be clearing the decks for a later improvement in earnings.
AT&T Chairman Robert Allen said that the company was targetting earning between $5 and $6 per share in five years time.
"There was a real emphasis on cost cutting," said Merrill Lynch's Toole.
AT&T shares were 1-1/2 lower at 38-3/8 at 0945 EST (1445 GMT).
